title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups's PR #385 review
description: Tracked, non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #385 (backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups, the same-ticker merge lost-update fix using PositionORM.version/version_id_col). These are independent of that review's one blocking finding (delete_position's new unhandled StaleDataError exposure, recorded on the parent task's own review.comments and sent back for a fix) -- none of the items below block the PR once that blocking item is addressed. Confirmed via a `code-review` skill pass run alongside the manual review, which independently corroborated two of these three items.

checklist.step: `_merge_and_commit`'s retry loop re-invokes `_merge_position` on every attempt, which re-fetches `provider.get_daily_ohlcv(existing.ticker)` (for `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`) each time -- but that fetch's result depends only on the ticker, not on the row's current merge state, so a merge that needs several retries to win under same-ticker contention re-issues the same OHLCV provider call several times instead of once. Likely cheap in practice (CachedDataProvider's warm-cache layer should absorb repeat calls within the same request's short retry window), but it's relying on that caching layer's incidental behavior rather than `_merge_and_commit` fetching the data once itself -- worth fetching once per `_merge_and_commit` call and passing it through, or at least an explicit `decisions` entry recording why relying on the cache is an acceptable tradeoff.

The new `test_retries_exhausted_returns_503_not_an_infinite_loop` test (backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py, class TestAddPositionMergeRetryBoundsAndRequeryHardening) doesn't assert the actual number of merge attempts made before giving up -- unlike its sibling tests in TestAddPositionMergeCommitRaceHandling, which do assert exact `call_count` values. As written, it would pass identically whether `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` were 1, 5, or 50, so it verifies there's SOME bound but doesn't actually pin down the retry-bound value the PR's own commentary describes testing. Add a call-count assertion (mirroring the existing `call_count["n"] == 2`/`== 3` pattern already used elsewhere in that same test module) to directly verify `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` attempts are made, not more or fewer.

Migration 051c44cc730b's round-trip behavior (upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade, including the `server_default` backfill of a pre-existing row's `version` to 1) was verified only by hand during this PR's review (pr-reviewer independently reproduced it manually against a scratch DB and confirmed it's clean) -- no automated test exercises this migration's downgrade/backfill path specifically. This matches existing precedent (no other migration in this codebase has a dedicated round-trip test either -- `test_db_migrations.py`'s `TestUpgradeHeadAgainstAFreshDatabase` only checks the fresh-upgrade-to-head column set), so it's not a new gap this PR introduces below the bar, but worth considering a small, shared downgrade/backfill-round-trip test helper for migrations that add a backfilled column, applied here and retroactively to earlier similar migrations (e.g. the ones adding `entry_notes`/`strategy`/`trailing_stop_high_water_mark` to `positions`), if that pattern recurs again.
